technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing Spring XD module-definition metadata and Javadoc conventions as the source for high-level descriptions, rather than introducing a new documentation format.
Document module descriptions in the locations consumed by both developers and users, with consistent terminology and links to the relevant module definitions.
Use the existing Spring XD build and packaging process to produce RPMs and publish them to the specified spring.io repository location.

Use RabbitMQ and Kafka performance-testing utilities already available in the project where possible; add only the scripts, configuration, and harness changes needed to make benchmark execution repeatable.
Define benchmark results using repeatable workload parameters such as message size, producer and consumer counts, batching, acknowledgements, persistence settings, throughput, and latency.
Use an EC2-based Kafka test topology modeled on the referenced Kafka engineering benchmark, while documenting deviations caused by the available AWS instance types or project environment.
Capture Kafka and Rabbit benchmark setup, execution commands, raw results, and conclusions as version-controlled documentation.
Document message-header compatibility changes between Spring XD 1.0 and 1.1 in the troubleshooting documentation, including likely serialization failure symptoms and remediation.
assumptions: The increment targets the Spring XD 1.1 release context described in the requirements.
The existing Spring XD source tree, build scripts, module definitions, RPM packaging configuration, and performance-testing utilities are available and buildable with limited unrelated repair work.
The developer has access to the required source repositories, AWS account, EC2 instances, RabbitMQ and Kafka environments, and spring.io repository credentials.
Publishing RPMs includes producing, validating, and uploading the artifacts, but not establishing a new repository or obtaining organizational approvals.
Benchmarking includes environment setup, repeatable test execution, data collection, analysis, and documentation; it does not require production-grade long-term monitoring.
AWS charges, infrastructure provisioning wait time, network provisioning delays, and external review or approval time are excluded from workday effort.
The requested Kafka baseline is a practical reproduction or approximation of the referenced benchmark, not an exact reproduction of LinkedIn's hardware and deployment environment.
Module descriptions can be derived from existing source and metadata without substantial redesign or implementation of new module capabilities.
One workday represents one person-day of productive development effort; the estimate is effort, not elapsed calendar duration.

activities.activity_description: Review the eight user stories, inspect the existing build, module metadata, packaging, benchmark utilities, documentation structure, and release conventions; define the implementation checklist and acceptance evidence.

Inspect each Spring XD module definition and related Javadoc, write or complete concise high-level descriptions covering purpose and capabilities, place them in the developer- and user-facing documentation locations, and verify links and formatting.

Compare the 1.0 and 1.1 message-header behavior and serialization representation, identify migration and troubleshooting implications for reused batch jobs, and document symptoms, causes, and corrective actions in the troubleshooting section.

activities.activity_name: Spring XD RPM build and repository publication
activities.activity_description: Validate or adjust RPM packaging, build the release RPM artifacts, verify package metadata and installation-level integrity, publish the artifacts to the specified spring.io release repository path, and record the publication details.

Define RabbitMQ benchmark scenarios and metrics, configure the test environment, run repeatable producer and consumer performance tests at representative loads, collect results, analyze throughput and relevant limitations, and document reference results for XD cluster setup.

activities.activity_name: Kafka EC2 infrastructure research and test-topology design
activities.activity_description: Research suitable EC2 instance types, storage, networking, broker count, client placement, operating-system requirements, and cost or capacity constraints; produce a concrete Kafka performance-test topology and provisioning checklist.

Identify and document broker, producer, consumer, topic, replication, batching, compression, acknowledgement, partitioning, JVM, and operating-system settings required for repeatable Kafka performance testing and comparison with the reference benchmark.

activities.activity_name: Kafka benchmark implementation, execution, and analysis
activities.activity_description: Configure the in-built Kafka performance-testing producer and consumer utilities, provision or validate the test environment, run baseline workloads, capture throughput and latency metrics, troubleshoot test issues, compare results with the reference baseline, and document reproducible procedures and findings.

activities.activity_name: Verification, integration review, and delivery cleanup
activities.activity_description: Build and smoke-test the affected project components, verify documentation references and published artifact availability, review benchmark scripts and results for reproducibility, resolve minor defects, and assemble the final increment notes.
